title: Outdoor Comfort Score vs Temperature Correlation
dataSources: Weather-station readings (`weatherstation:reading`), daily weather-impact rollups (`personalweather:daily`), sleep correlation records (`personalweather:sleep`), step correlation records (`personalweather:steps`), mood correlation records (`personalweather:mood`).
app: Local weather-station readings correlated with personal sleep, steps, mood, and outdoor-activity summaries in Splunk via scripted inputs and daily rollups.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=personalweather:daily
| stats avg(outdoor_comfort_score) as metric_value avg(temp_c) as avg_temp by day
| stats corr(metric_value, avg_temp) as corr_value
description: Measures how strongly outdoor comfort score moves with local temperature across your daily weather-impact rollups.
value: Temperature correlation is the fastest way to test whether a weather hunch about outdoor comfort score is real or just memorable.
implementation: Build one daily record per day with both the personal metric and matched weather fields before running the correlation.
visualization: Single-value correlation panel for outdoor comfort score versus temperature.
grandmaExplanation: It nudges whether hotter or colder weather usually goes along with better or worse outdoor comfort score.
